simple.meaning: רָשָׁע (râshâʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “morally wrong ; concretely, an (actively) bad person.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 263 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, and 5 more, beginning at Genesis 18:23. Its contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָשָׁע (H7563).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָשָׁע (râshâʻ) / H7563 is traced through Genesis 18:23, Genesis 18:25, Exodus 2:13, Exodus 9:27 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Abraham came near, and said, “Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?

May it be far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”

May it be far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”
He went out the second day, and behold, two men of the Hebrews were fighting with each other. He said to him who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your fellow?”
Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and Aaron, and said to them, “I have sinned this time. Yahweh is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
“You shall not spread a false report. Don’t join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
“Keep far from a false charge, and don’t kill the innocent and righteous; for I will not justify the wicked.
He spoke to the congregation, saying, “Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be consumed in all their sins!”
“ ‘Moreover you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death. He shall surely be put to death.
If there is a controversy between men, and they come to judgment and the judges judge them, then they shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked.
It shall be, if the wicked man is worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down and to be beaten before his face, according to his wickedness, by number.
He will keep the feet of his holy ones,
How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house on his bed, should I not now require his blood from your hand, and rid the earth of you?”
then hear in heaven, and act, and judge your servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way on his own head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
then hear from heaven, act, and judge your servants, bringing retribution to the wicked, to bring his way on his own head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked, and love those who hate Yahweh? Because of this, wrath is on you from before Yahweh.
There the wicked cease from troubling.
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame.
“It is all the same.
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.

definitions.full: H7563. rasha רָשָׁע 263 adjective wicked, criminal ; — absolute ׳ר Gen 18:23 +; plural רְשָׁעִים Isa 13:11 +; construct רִשְׁעֵי Psa 75:9 3 t. feminine singular רְשָׁעָה Ezek 3:18 (strike out Co), 3:19 ( רָשָׁע Co); — 1 usually as substantive , one guilty of crime , deserving punishment; sometimes also wicked ; opposed to צַדִּיע ; רָשָׁע Exod 2:13 ; 23:1 (E), Deut 25:2 ; Prov 17:23 ; 18:5 ; 25:5 ; Job 9:22 , 24 ; collective Gen 18:23 , 25 (twice in verse) (J) Micah 6:10 ; Prov 3:33 ; 28:4 , רשׁעים 1Sam 24:14 ; Jer 5:26 ; Prov 19:28 ; 20:26 ; 29:12 , רשׁעים אנשׁים 2Sam 4:11 (murderers), לָמוּת רָשָׁע Num 35:31 (P) guilty of death , ר ׳מוֺשֵׁל Prov 28:15 , compare 29:2 , ר ׳הִצְדִּיק Exod 23:7 (E) Isa 5:23 ; Prov 17:15 ; ר ׳הִרְשִׁיעַ Deut 25:1 ; 1Kin 8:32 = לְרָשָׁע השׁיב 2Chr 6:23 ; לר ׳אמר צַדִּיק Prov 24:24 . 2 guilty of hostility to God or his people, wicked enemies: רשׁע singular Psa 17:13 6 t. Psalms; Isa 26:10 ; collective Psa 9:6 ; 9:17 ; 10:2 6 t. Psalms; Isa 11:4 ; Hab 3:13 ; רשׁעים Psa 3:8 ; 7:10 ; 9:18 5 t. Psalms; Isa 48:22 ; 57:20-21 , Jer 25:31 ; Ezekiel 21:34; Malachi 3:21 ( + (possibly) other cases; often hard to decide); specifically of Pharaoh Exod 9:27 (J), Babylon Isa 13:11 ; 14:5 , Chaldeans Hab 1:4 , 13 ; || יהוה שׂנְאֵי 2Chr 19:2 . 3 guilty of sin , against either God or man, wicked: הרשׁעים האנשׁים Num 16:26 (J, rebellious Korahites), Mal 3:18 (not serving ׳י ), opposed to צַדִּיק ; singular individual Ezek 3:18 (twice in verse); 21:30 ; 33:8 (twice in verse); Psa 11:5 ; 32:10 ; Prov 9:7 +; collective Isa 3:11 ; Job 34:18 ; 36:6 , 17 ; plural רשׁעים Isa 53:9 ; Jer 23:19 = 30:23 , Zeph 1:3 ; Psa 26:5 ; Prov 10:3 ; Eccl 8:10 +; || חסֹידים 1Sam 2:9 (Poem), Psalm 12:9; Psa 50:16 ; 97:10 ; 145:20 ; || תוֺדָתֶ֑ךָ עֹזְבֵי 119:53 ; compare V:61, +; ר ׳אדם Prov 11:7 ; Job 20:29 ; 27:13 ; ר ׳אִישׁ Prov 21:29 ; ר ׳מלאך 13:17 ; רשׁעים זֶרַע Psa 37:28 ; רשׁעים עֲצַת 1:1 ; Job 10:3 ; 21:16 ; 22:18 ; רשׁעים דֶּרֶךְ Jer 12:1 ; Psa 1:6 ; 146:9 ; Prov 4:19 ; 12:26 ; רשׁע דֶּרֶךְ 15:9 ; הָֽרְשָׁעה מִדַּדְכּוֺ Ezek 3:18-19 , (but see, Co, above); (ה)ארץ רִשְׁעֵי Psa 75:9 ; 101:8 ; 119:119 ; Ezek 7:21 ( ᵐ5 Co עריצי ). — is rare before exile; chiefly Ezekiel Psalms Wisdom Literature.
